rv.q: In its ability to make us pause and face the monster head-on, Prometheus Firebringer is a quietly stunning, brain-jangling piece of work.
Behind the philosophical inquiries she puts onstage, there is real intelligence at play.
To say that Annie Dorsen’s Prometheus Firebringer checks all the boxes is an understatement of what she has done here.
Half of what happens in “Prometheus Firebringer” is extraordinary, unprecedented.
Intellectually speaking, Dorsen’s points are compelling and well-taken. Theatrically speaking, it’s a desert on both sides of the stage.
There’s brilliance at hand here but such demanding brilliance that an all-fired-up observer pausing to think about what’s just occurred can be distracted from what’s now occurring.
Taken altogether, Dorsen makes a compelling case for the power of AI as both an innovative tool as well as a potential threat.

cn.t: Dorsen's provocative hybrid lecture-performance exploring AI and ancient Greek tragedy earns mixed-to-positive reviews. Critics praise its intellectual ambition and timeliness, though some find the staging less compelling than the ideas.
